stated.text: It is a Node.js app with no npm dependencies.
`node server.js` serves the app on the port in the PORT environment variable, default 3000.
GET / is the app.
Everything the app keeps lives under the folder named by the DATA_DIR environment variable (default `./data`), so it survives a restart.
Every assistant reply comes from the stand-in in `provider/`, used as it is and not changed (not edited, copied or replaced).
The records the assistant may work with are the synthetic ones in `records/`; a person may read, and ask to change, only the records that list them as a reader.

The app keeps its own working copy of the records under its data folder, so a confirmed change survives a restart; `records/people.json` and `records/records.json` stay as they are, and starting with an empty data folder gives the starting state again.
A record a person creates is theirs: its `readers` is that person alone, and a new order's `id` is the next free `ORD-` number.
I can open the app, ask for help in ordinary language and get a reply.
The conversation is the center of the experience, with polished typography, comfortable reading and clear composition.
When I ask a follow-up, the bot understands the conversation (earlier turns of this conversation reach the reply).
The bot asks a useful clarifying question when needed, and my next message is taken as the answer to it.
I can name my bots.
I can keep multiple saved conversations and return to the right bot and discussion without losing my place.
I can save reusable instructions, use them again and change them.
I can save reusable tasks, use them again and change them.
I can inspect what a bot remembers about me.
I can correct a mistake in what a bot remembers about me.
I can ask a bot to forget something, and it is removed from what that bot remembers about me.
Asking a bot to remember something adds it to what that bot remembers about me.
My information stays separate from another user's.
Each bot's memory stays separate from my other bots.
Questions about the records get accurate answers grounded only in records I am allowed to read, and I can follow up naturally.
When I ask to create or update something, I see the exact proposed changes before deciding.
Nothing is written until I explicitly confirm the proposal.
Rejecting or cancelling a proposal leaves the records alone.
Repeating an action or reloading at an awkward moment does not apply it twice.
I am told what actually happened to a proposal.
Longer tasks continue doing useful work while the app is closed.
When I return, I get an honest account of what finished, what is still happening and anything that needs my attention.
I can steer ongoing work with a follow-up (the added step joins the end of my running task in this conversation).
I can cancel ongoing work, with a clear explanation of what can still be stopped and what has already happened.
If something fails or is interrupted, the app helps me recover without guessing or losing the conversation.
Setup is guided and recoverable and explains what I need without exposing secrets.
Everyday use is comfortable on a desktop, in a narrow window and with the keyboard.
There are no passwords. The first screen offers a button named Continue as <name> for each person in `records/people.json`.
After continuing, a button named Switch person brings the first screen back.
What I see, and what my bots remember, belongs to the person I continued as.
Reloading the page keeps me as the person I continued as.
At a desktop width (1440 pixels) everything named in the request is on the main screen without opening a menu.
In a narrow window parts may be folded away, but reading the conversation and writing a message stay in view.
When no provider token has been saved, a region named Setup explains what is needed, with a textbox named Provider token and a button named Save token.
A token the provider refuses shows an alert and lets me try again.
A token in the PROVIDER_TOKEN environment variable counts as saved.
Once saved, the token is never shown again, in any page or any response.
A navigation named Bots lists my bots as buttons named with each bot's name, with the open one marked as current.
A button named New bot, a textbox named Bot name and a button named Save bot name create a bot and open it.
A button named Rename bot uses the Bot name textbox and Save bot name button to rename the open bot.
A person who has never used the app starts with one bot named Assistant.
A navigation named Conversations lists the open bot's conversations as buttons, with the open one marked as current.
A button named New conversation starts a conversation.
A region named Conversation holds the messages as articles named Message from <name>, with my name or the bot's name.
A textbox named Message and a button named Send write to the conversation.
In the Message textbox, Enter sends and Shift+Enter makes a new line.
While a reply is on its way, a status says so.
If a reply fails, an alert says so and a button named Retry tries again without sending my message a second time.
A region named Saved instructions has textboxes named Instruction name and Instruction text and a button named Save instruction.
Each saved instruction has buttons named Use <name>, Edit <name> and Delete <name>.
Using a saved instruction makes it the open bot's instructions from the next reply on.
Edit <name> on an instruction puts it back into the Instruction name and Instruction text textboxes, to change and save again under the same name.
Delete <name> on an instruction removes it.
A region named Saved tasks has textboxes named Task name and Task request and a button named Save task.
Each saved task has buttons named Run <name>, Edit <name> and Delete <name>.
Running a saved task sends its request in the open conversation.
Edit <name> on a task puts it back into the Task name and Task request textboxes, to change and save again under the same name.
Delete <name> on a task removes it.
A region named Memory lists what the open bot remembers about me as list items, each with buttons named Edit memory and Forget.
Editing a memory uses a textbox named Memory text and a button named Save memory.
A proposal appears in a region named Proposed changes that states each change exactly (for example `ORD-1001 status: open → closed`), with buttons named Confirm changes and Reject changes.
After a proposal is decided, a region named Change result says what happened.
A region named Tasks shows each long task as an article named Task: <title>.
Each task article holds a status named Task status that reads Running, Completed, Failed, Cancelled or Interrupted.
Each task article shows the steps that have finished.
Each task article has a button named Cancel task while it runs.
Each task article has a button named Retry task after a failure or an interruption.
When I come back after being away, a region named Since you were away tells me what finished, what is still running and what needs my attention.
The rules the app follows are in modules it uses, covered by node:test tests under test/ that `npm test` runs.

unstated.text: Whether saved instructions and saved tasks belong to the person (shared by all their bots) or to one bot.
unstated.why: A person with several bots expects to find, or not find, a saved instruction after switching bot; another person must never see them either way.
unstated.probe: Continue as Maya; in bot Assistant save instruction 'Brief' with text 'Be brief'; create bot 'Second' and open it; look at the Saved instructions region; then Switch person, Continue as Theo and look again.
unstated.fine_answers: Shared across one person's bots, or per bot, as long as it is consistent and never visible to another person.

unstated.text: What happens to a bot's instructions when the saved instruction it uses is later edited or deleted.
unstated.why: The person changes an instruction 'when needs change' and needs to know whether the bot that uses it follows the change or keeps the old text.
unstated.probe: Save instruction 'Tone' = 'Be formal'; click Use Tone; send 'who are you'; Edit Tone to 'Be casual' and save; send 'who are you'; then Delete Tone and send 'who are you' again.
unstated.fine_answers: The bot follows the saved instruction (edit updates, delete clears) or keeps a copy taken at Use; either if what the bot now uses is visible or explained.

unstated.text: Whether a bot's instructions can be cleared or seen, and what the bot uses before any instruction is applied.
unstated.why: Once an instruction is applied there is no stated way to go back to no instructions or to see which one a bot is using.
unstated.probe: Use a saved instruction on a bot; look for any indication of which instruction the open bot uses and any way to remove it; send 'who are you'.
unstated.fine_answers: A shown current instruction with a way to clear it, or deleting the saved one clears it; any honest, discoverable route.

unstated.text: What Save instruction or Save task does when the name already exists and Edit was not used, or when name or text is empty.
unstated.why: Two entries with the same name give duplicate Use/Run/Edit/Delete button names and an ambiguous target; an empty one gives buttons named 'Use '.
unstated.probe: Save instruction 'A' = 'x'; save instruction 'A' = 'y' without pressing Edit; count the Use A buttons and check which text applies; then try to save with an empty name and with empty text.
unstated.fine_answers: Overwrite, refuse with a message, or ask; empty fields refused. Not two entries with one name.

unstated.text: How empty, blank or duplicate bot names are handled.
unstated.why: Bots are listed as buttons named with each bot's name, so a blank or repeated name makes the list unreadable and ambiguous to a screen reader.
unstated.probe: Click New bot, leave Bot name empty and click Save bot name; then create a second bot named Assistant; inspect the Bots navigation.
unstated.fine_answers: Refuse with a message, or allow duplicates but keep each bot distinguishable; blank names refused.

unstated.text: How conversations are named and ordered in the Conversations list.
unstated.why: Returning to 'the right discussion' requires telling conversations apart; buttons all called 'Conversation' do not.
unstated.probe: In one bot start three conversations, sending a different first message in each; read the button names and order in the Conversations navigation.
unstated.fine_answers: Named by first message, by time, or by a title; any order that lets the person find a conversation.

unstated.text: Whether bots and conversations can be deleted.
unstated.why: The request asks for many bots and conversations but no way to remove one; a list that only grows becomes hard to use.
unstated.probe: Create a bot and a conversation, then look for any way to remove each.
unstated.fine_answers: A delete control, or none, if the absence is a deliberate choice the delivery states.

unstated.text: Which bot and conversation are open after reloading, after Switch person and back, and after a server restart; and whether an unsent draft in the Message box survives.
unstated.why: 'Returning without losing my place' needs a defined place; a draft lost on reload is a common annoyance.
unstated.probe: As Maya open bot Second, conversation 2; type an unsent message; reload; then Switch person to Theo and back to Maya; then restart the server and reload.
unstated.fine_answers: Last-open bot and conversation restored per person; draft kept or not, as long as the place is.

unstated.text: Whether the person's identity is checked by the server on every request, or only chosen in the page.
unstated.why: 'My information stays separate' fails if a request naming another person's bot, conversation, memory, task or proposal is served or acted on.
unstated.probe: As Maya note the id of a conversation (from the page's network requests); Switch person to Ana; replay the request for Maya's conversation, memory or a confirm of Maya's proposal with Ana's session; check the response and the records.
unstated.fine_answers: Refused (403/404) or empty; any answer that never returns or changes another person's data.

unstated.text: Whether a proposal that changes `readers`, `id`, `type` or `owner` is offered and applied.
unstated.why: The stand-in proposes 'set the readers of ORD-1001 to ana'; applying it would let a person grant or remove someone else's access, or lose their own, breaking the read rules.
unstated.probe: As Maya send 'set the readers of ORD-1001 to ana' and confirm; then send 'set the id of ORD-1004 to ORD-9999' and confirm; check which records Maya, Theo and Ana can read.
unstated.fine_answers: Refused with an explanation, or allowed only with a clear warning; not silently changing who may read a record.

unstated.text: Whether a proposed field value is validated (a word into a number field, a field the record does not have, an unknown status).
unstated.why: The stand-in turns 'set the total of ORD-1001 to lots' into a text total and proposes adding fields that do not exist (from nothing); a bad value then shows up in later answers.
unstated.probe: As Maya send 'set the total of ORD-1001 to lots' and confirm; send 'set the colour of ORD-1001 to red' and confirm; ask 'what is the total of ORD-1001'.
unstated.fine_answers: Refuse or warn before confirm, or apply what was shown exactly; either if the proposal states the exact change.

unstated.text: What Confirm does when the record changed after the proposal was made (another reader changed it, or an earlier proposal on the same field was confirmed).
unstated.why: ORD-1001 is shared by Maya and Theo; confirming 'open → closed' when it is already 'shipped' would silently overwrite the other person's change.
unstated.probe: As Maya send 'set the status of ORD-1001 to closed' (do not confirm); in another browser as Theo send 'set the status of ORD-1001 to shipped' and confirm; back as Maya click Confirm changes; read Change result and ask 'what is the status of ORD-1001'.
unstated.fine_answers: Refuse as stale and offer a new proposal, or apply with Change result stating the actual from-value; not a silent overwrite reported as 'open → closed'.

unstated.text: Whether an undecided proposal survives reload, restart and later messages, and whether an older proposal can still be confirmed after a newer one appears.
unstated.why: A reload 'at an awkward moment' should neither lose the decision nor let a stale proposal be applied by accident.
unstated.probe: Get a proposal; reload; restart the server and reload; then send another proposal request without deciding the first; try Confirm on each.
unstated.fine_answers: Kept and decidable, or expired with a clear message; never applied without a confirm and never applied twice.

unstated.text: How the next free ORD- number is chosen when two create proposals are pending at once, or two people create orders.
unstated.why: Two new orders must not get the same id; a gap or reuse after a rejected proposal also confuses people.
unstated.probe: As Maya send 'create an order for X totalling 10' and, without confirming, as Ana send 'create an order for Y totalling 20'; confirm both; list ids with 'what is the customer of ORD-1005' and 'ORD-1006' as each person.
unstated.fine_answers: Number assigned at confirm time, or reserved at proposal; distinct ids either way.

unstated.text: Whether the Change result stays visible after reload and how confirmed changes are recorded in the conversation.
unstated.why: 'Understand what actually happened' after a reload at the awkward moment requires the outcome to persist, not only flash once.
unstated.probe: Confirm a proposal and reload immediately; click Confirm again if still offered; look for the Change result and the conversation's record of it.
unstated.fine_answers: Result kept in the conversation or region; any persistent, honest account.

unstated.text: What Retry does after a reload or server restart, and what happens to the failed message if I send a new one instead.
unstated.why: A failed message must not vanish or be sent twice; the stand-in's `[fail once]` succeeds only when the attempt number rises, so a reset attempt count fails forever.
unstated.probe: Send 'hello [fail once]'; at the alert, reload the page, then click Retry; repeat with a server restart before Retry; separately, at the alert send 'next' instead of Retry and inspect the messages.
unstated.fine_answers: Retry still offered and succeeds, or the failed message is marked failed with a way to resend; never duplicated, never lost.

unstated.text: What happens if I send again, switch conversation or reload while a reply is still on its way.
unstated.why: Double-clicking Send or sending during a slow reply can duplicate messages or attach a reply to the wrong conversation.
unstated.probe: Send 'hello [slow]' and press Enter again immediately; send another '[slow]' message and switch to a different conversation, then back; send one and reload during the wait.
unstated.fine_answers: Send disabled while pending, or messages queued in order; the reply lands in its own conversation and is kept after reload.

unstated.text: Whether a memory 'forget' that matches nothing, or a repeated 'remember', is reported honestly and kept tidy.
unstated.why: The stand-in always says 'I've forgotten ...' even when no fact matches, and repeats a remembered fact; the person would believe something was forgotten that was not.
unstated.probe: Send 'remember that I like tea' twice; open Memory; send 'forget coffee'; check the Memory list and whether the app says nothing was removed.
unstated.fine_answers: Duplicates merged or shown; a non-matching forget flagged (or matched loosely and shown); the Memory list is the truth.

unstated.text: What Save memory does with empty text, and whether Forget asks for confirmation or can be undone.
unstated.why: Saving an empty memory leaves a blank list item; a mistaken Forget loses a fact with no way back.
unstated.probe: Click Edit memory on an item, clear Memory text, click Save memory; click Forget on another item; look for a confirmation or undo.
unstated.fine_answers: Empty refused or treated as forget; Forget immediate or confirmed; either if stated.

unstated.text: Which long tasks the Tasks region shows: the open conversation's, the open bot's, or all of the person's.
unstated.why: A task started in another conversation or bot must still be findable and cancellable, and must never show to another person.
unstated.probe: As Maya start 'long task: report [long]' in conversation 1; open conversation 2 and another bot; look at Tasks; Switch person to Theo and look again.
unstated.fine_answers: All of the person's tasks, or the conversation's with a way to reach others; never another person's.

unstated.text: Whether a finished, failed or cancelled task leaves a message in its conversation.
unstated.why: The conversation is 'the center of the experience'; a result only in the Tasks panel may be missed and is not part of the follow-up context.
unstated.probe: Start 'long task: notes' and wait for Completed; read the Conversation region; then ask a follow-up.
unstated.fine_answers: A bot message with the result, or the result only in the task article; either if findable after reload.

unstated.text: What the app does with a running task when the server stops and starts again: mark it Interrupted, resume it, or both.
unstated.why: Work is meant to continue while the app is closed; after a crash or restart the person needs to know whether steps will be redone or need Retry.
unstated.probe: Start 'long task: audit [long]'; after two steps finish, stop the server; start it again; reload and read Task status, the finished steps, Since you were away, and whether it continues on its own.
unstated.fine_answers: Interrupted with Retry task, or resumed automatically from the next unfinished step; done steps not lost or silently redone.

unstated.text: Whether Retry task resumes at the failed step or starts the task over.
unstated.why: Redoing steps that already finished wastes work and contradicts the 'steps that have finished' list.
unstated.probe: Start 'long task: plan [fail step 2]'; wait for Failed; click Retry task; read the step list and count 'Done:' entries for step 1.
unstated.fine_answers: Resume at the failed step (likely expected) or rerun all with the list made clear.

unstated.text: What Cancel task does to a step that is in progress, and how the account separates 'already happened' from 'stopped'.
unstated.why: The request asks for a clear explanation of what can still be stopped; a step mid-flight may finish anyway.
unstated.probe: Start 'long task: big [long]' with STANDIN_STEP_MS=3000; click Cancel task mid-step; read Task status, finished steps and the explanation; wait a few seconds and read again.
unstated.fine_answers: The in-flight step finishes and is listed then the task stops, or it is discarded and said so; status ends Cancelled and stays so.

unstated.text: What 'add step:' does when no task is running in the conversation, or when several are.
unstated.why: The stand-in replies 'I'll add ... to the task that is running' regardless; saying it was added when there is no task is dishonest.
unstated.probe: In a conversation with no running task send 'add step: double-check'; then start two long tasks in one conversation and send 'add step: extra'; read both task articles.
unstated.fine_answers: Tell the person there is nothing to add to; with several, add to the latest or ask which; never claim an addition that did not happen.

unstated.text: What counts as 'being away' for the Since you were away region, and when it goes.
unstated.why: Shown on every load it is noise; shown never it hides what finished; it must be per person.
unstated.probe: As Maya start a long task, close the tab, wait until it completes, reopen; read Since you were away; reload again; Switch person to Ana and check it shows only Ana's work.
unstated.fine_answers: Since the person's last visit, dismissed on reading or after a reload; any rule that shows new events once and only the person's own.

unstated.text: Who may save or replace the provider token, and which wins when PROVIDER_TOKEN and a saved token differ.
unstated.why: The token belongs to whoever runs the app, not the people using it; any person replacing it, or an env token silently ignored, affects everyone.
unstated.probe: Start with PROVIDER_TOKEN set to a valid token and check Setup is absent; start with an invalid PROVIDER_TOKEN and see what Setup shows; save a token as Maya then Switch person to Theo and look for a way to change it.
unstated.fine_answers: One app-wide token with Setup shown before or after choosing a person; env first or saved first, if stated; replacement possible or not, if stated.

unstated.text: What happens when the saved token later stops being accepted (changed environment or bad env value) during use.
unstated.why: 'Recoverable setup' means a refused token at reply time leads back to Setup rather than an endless failing Retry.
unstated.probe: Start with PROVIDER_TOKEN=sk-local-short (refused); send a message; read the alert and whether Setup is offered.
unstated.fine_answers: Alert plus a route back to Setup; any route that does not expose the token.

unstated.text: Whether the token is stored in plain text under DATA_DIR and whether it leaks into logs or error messages.
unstated.why: The token must never be shown in any response; a stack trace or log line with it, or a copied data folder, exposes it to the operator's audience.
unstated.probe: Save a token; grep the server output, every API response and the files under DATA_DIR for the token text; trigger a provider error and read the alert.
unstated.fine_answers: Stored on disk is fine if never sent to the browser or logged; plain or obscured storage, if stated.

unstated.text: What the app does when the data folder is unwritable or holds damaged files at start.
unstated.why: Everything lives under DATA_DIR; an operator needs an error that says what is wrong rather than a silent reset that loses conversations.
unstated.probe: Start with DATA_DIR pointing to a read-only folder; then put invalid JSON in one of the app's data files and start again.
unstated.fine_answers: Refuse to start with a clear message, or start and report the problem; not silently discarding data.

unstated.text: How the app behaves when Switch person happens while a reply is pending or a proposal is undecided.
unstated.why: A reply or proposal started as Maya must not appear for Theo or be confirmable by him.
unstated.probe: As Maya send 'set the status of ORD-1001 to closed [slow]'; click Switch person and Continue as Theo before the reply arrives; look at what Theo sees; switch back to Maya.
unstated.fine_answers: The reply and proposal land only in Maya's conversation; Theo sees nothing of them.
